title: Das Johannesbuch der Mandäer (German, Lidzbarski 1915)
author: Mark Lidzbarski
description: Das Johannesbuch der Mandäer (The Book of John of the Mandaeans), the Mandaic text with German translation, introduction and commentary by Mark Lidzbarski (Giessen: Alfred Töpelmann, 1915). The Drashe d-Yahya (Discourses of John), also called the Book of Kings, is one of the principal holy books of the Mandaeans, the Gnostic baptist community of southern Iraq and Iran. It contains discourses, dialogues and legends centred on Yahya-Yohana (John the Baptist), presented as a prophet of the Great Life, his baptism of the faithful in living water, his debates with priests and with the Messiah, and his ascent to the world of light, together with teachings on the beings of light, the soul and the fight against the demons of darkness. Lidzbarski's edition founded modern study of this text and was the basis of G. R. S. Mead's English selections in The Gnostic John the Baptizer.
